scope: Administrator identity separation from content, followed by removal of one redundant dashboard profile read.

measurement.environment: Owned KVM lab, 8192 MiB / 4 vCPUs, eight backends with one Ready replica each; dev stopped throughout.
measurement.data: Same retained DEMO database and canonical admin-demo-ava actor; no fixture reset. Own native sessions are created and revoked. Background telemetry/session state can evolve.
measurement.workload: Seven validated admin GET routes, four concurrent closed-loop clients; each round has 30 s warmup, 10 s post-warmup quiet interval, 30 s measured load.
measurement.reproduction: python3 microservices/tools/check-load.py --profile admin-identity --seconds 30 --warmup-seconds 30 --concurrency 4 --output <report.json> (three serial rounds on each source; all backends stopped before image replacement)
measurement.baselineBuild: Exact detached fad15dced source, freshly built with backend-dirty=false. Retained old images were not accepted as source-proven baseline.
measurement.initialCandidateBuild: d6413a84b source. Images were built before that commit, so OCI labels retain its parent revision with backend-dirty=true.
measurement.fixedCandidateBuild: d6413a84b plus the exact canonical source patch below; OCI backend-dirty=true. Other uncommitted edits are measurement tooling, tests, AGENTS and the image lock.
measurement.cpuUnits: One cpuCores unit is one fully occupied logical CPU. hostBusyPercent covers all host logical CPUs. Per-request QEMU CPU uses the complete measured cpu.time delta divided by validated requests.
limitations: All round results are retained. JVM warmup remains visible across rounds; these medians do not prove steady-state or universal performance.
CPU snapshots use per-container crictl inspection; intervals include roughly 1.5-2 seconds of measurement overhead. Both sources use the same instrumentation.
The 10-second quiet interval follows warmup and is not settled idle. Host CPU includes unrelated desktop processes; QEMU CPU isolates the VM process.
This is end-to-end native HTTP latency, not isolated Mongo query timing. The focused regression proves removal of one redundant profile read.
This does not qualify whole-community omission, template installation, browser rendering or every business flow.

transportJUnit.execution: Retained successful result; unchanged Gradle transport test task was UP-TO-DATE during the final build

performanceUnitTests.command: python3 -m unittest discover -s microservices/tools -p test_infra.py -k PerformanceEvidenceTest

interpretation: Final median overall throughput improves and CPU per request decreases. Dashboard median p95 remains above baseline (95.16 to 104.01 ms); individual matched rounds are 148.17/95.16/78.11 before versus 135.61/104.01/75.45 after. This mixed warming result does not establish universal speedup or performance parity.
